audit_findings.title: Cash bridge may treat customer advances as excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; $547.889 million of cash/STI was added while contract liabilities were $627.020 million, including a $113.051 million six-month increase
audit_findings.mechanism: The equity bridge adds cash as surplus even though customer advances and bonding requirements may make part of it operating capital required to complete contracts.
audit_findings.evidence: The temporary increase in contract liabilities of $214.7 million represented a source of cash, primarily due to the net effect of the early phase of construction activities on certain projects.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that customer advances materially funded liquidity and that significant liquid capital supports bonding. They do not establish how much of the $547.889 million is distributable. Because the entire bridge addition equals 25.3% of base equity value, the unresolved classification is material.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile cash, CDs and other investments by project against contract liabilities, remaining contract costs, restricted or pledged funds and minimum bonding liquidity; rerun all scenarios using only evidenced excess cash.

audit_findings.title: The FY2026 anchor may retain nonrecurring tax benefits
audit_findings.magnitude: $16.772 million, comprising a $14.742 million SBC tax windfall and $2.030 million valuation-allowance benefit; 14.6% of the $115.2 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained, nonrecurring tax benefits inflate after-tax owner earnings and every forecast and terminal-value year derived from the anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: This tax rate differed from the statutory federal tax rate of 21% due to the favorable effects of the windfall benefit from stock-based compensation and the change in valuation allowance for NOLs.
audit_findings.explanation: The nonrecurring benefits are demonstrated in the filed tax reconciliation, but the record does not show whether the OE workpaper removed them. If both remain, their $16.772 million scale is large enough to materially affect operating value.
audit_findings.action: Trace the tax provision used in the OE calculation, remove the identified nonrecurring benefits if retained, apply an evidenced sustainable operating tax rate and rerun every scenario.

audit_findings.title: Latest-actual OE may capitalize a favorable project mix
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; FY2026 gross margin was 20.5% versus 16.1% in FY2025, a 4.4-point difference equal to $41.6 million at FY2026 revenue, while the latest six-month margin was 20.1%
audit_findings.mechanism: A temporarily elevated project margin would inflate the OE anchor and therefore forecast earnings and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase in gross profit margin between periods was primarily attributable to the changing mix of projects and contract types.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that project mix and execution raised margins, but it does not quantify catch-up gains or establish a normalized margin. The latest six-month margin of 20.1% shows some persistence, so the record cannot establish that FY2026 was erroneous or how material any normalization would be.
audit_findings.action: Obtain project-level margin bridges, cumulative catch-up adjustments and current backlog margin estimates; rerun the valuation only after quantifying the sustainable portion of the FY2026 margin.

audit_findings.title: Large bonded obligations remain outside recorded OE until losses become probable
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified loss exposure; filed unsatisfied bonded performance obligations were approximately $0.9 billion and other-risk bonds were $104.3 million at July 31, 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: A project failure could create completion costs or surety-reimbursement claims that reduce future OE or require an equity-bridge deduction once probable and estimable.
audit_findings.evidence: As of January 31, 2026, the estimated amount of the Company’s unsatisfied bonded performance obligations covering all subsidiaries was approximately $ 0.5 billion.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed bond amounts are performance limits, not loss estimates, and no present excess loss is established. The exposure is nevertheless large and has increased from $0.5 billion at January 31, making it a material forward-looking risk requiring surveillance rather than a current valuation adjustment.
audit_findings.action: Monitor project loss indicators, surety claims, collateral demands and cost-to-complete revisions; rerun when a project-specific probability and loss amount become supportable.

audit_findings.title: The disputed $10 million bond draw may require an equity haircut
audit_findings.magnitude: $9.8 million at July 31, 2026, equal to $0.69 per diluted share and 0.45% of the $2.166 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Non-recovery would require writing off the recorded receivable and would reduce equity value through a one-time claim not represented in normalized OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Subsequently, the project owner made a draw for the full amount of a $ 10.0 million irrevocable letter of credit, or on-demand performance bond, issued by the Company’s bank.
audit_findings.explanation: Recoverability remains disputed, but complete loss of the identified $9.8 million receivable would reduce base value from $152.20 to approximately $151.51 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion. Any additional counterclaim exposure is unquantified and is not established by the identified draw amount.
audit_findings.action: Confirm litigation status and receivable recoverability; apply the $9.8 million write-off sensitivity, and reassess separately if filed evidence quantifies an additional counterclaim exposure.

audit_findings.title: Deferred-compensation settlement terms could leave an omitted claim
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; total FY2026 contractual obligations were filed as less than $20.0 million, but the deferred-compensation portion and potential share count were not disclosed
audit_findings.mechanism: Share settlement would increase the fully diluted denominator, while cash settlement would reduce the cash properly available for the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company also maintains a nonqualified plan whereunder key employees may elect to defer portions of their compensation for periods ranging from one year to retirement.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing says contractual and deferred-compensation obligations were recorded as liabilities, but it does not establish settlement mechanics, participant balances or whether all potentially issuable shares are included in the 14.234463 million denominator. The less-than-$20 million aggregate disclosure does not isolate or bound every share-settlement outcome.
audit_findings.action: Inspect both plan documents and participant statements, reconcile cash-settled balances to recorded liabilities and add any omitted share-settled units to a rerun of the diluted denominator.
